Athens B.C.|AEK Athens]] | highlights = * [[EuroChallenge]] champion ([[2011–12 FIBA EuroChallenge|2012]]) * [[EuroChallenge Final Four MVP]] ([[2011–12 FIBA EuroChallenge|2012]]) * [[Turkish Cup Basketball|Turkish Cup]] champion ([[2011–12 Turkish Cup Basketball|2012]]) * [[Turkish Basketball League|TBL]] champion ([[2011–12 Turkish Basketball League|2012]]) * TBL Player of the Year (2012) * TBL Defensive Player of the Year (2012) * [[VTB United League]] champion ([[2009–10 VTB United League|2010]]) * [[NBA D-League]] All-Star Game MVP (2007) * First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2006) * Second-team All-Atlantic 10 (2005) }} '''Nana Papa Yaw''' "'''Pops'''" '''Mensah-Bonsu''' (born 7 September 1983) is a British basketball executive and former player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[George Washington University]] and professionally for five [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) teams as well as clubs in Spain, France, Turkey, Russia, Italy, Israel, and Greece. On an international level, he represented [[Great Britain men's national basketball team|Great Britain]] and was a member of [[Team GB]] at the [[2012 Summer Olympics|London 2012 Olympic Games]]. He also served as general manager of the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]] from 2018 to 2020. Throughout his career, he was known for his saying "No Mercy" after blocking a shot. A documentary entitled "No Mercy", was released at the end of his career, documenting his ups and downs and him being known for being a "less heralded" player by the media. ==Early life== Born and raised in London, Mensah-Bonsu, whose parents are from [[Ghana]], attended [[St Thomas More Catholic School, Wood Green|St. Thomas More Roman Catholic School]]. As a teenager, he represented the [[London Borough of Haringey]] at the [[London Youth Games]], appearing in four of Great Britain's five games.{{Cite web |last=Cooper |first=Ian |date=18 December 2012 |title=Tottenham Olympic basketball star hopes to inspire a generation |url=http://www.tottenhamjournal.co.uk/news/tottenham_olympic_basketball_star_hopes_to_inspire_a_generation_1_1744723 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130105002924/http://www.tottenhamjournal.co.uk/news/tottenham_olympic_basketball_star_hopes_to_inspire_a_generation_1_1744723 |archive-date=5 January 2013 |access-date=31 August 2013 |website=TottenhamJournal.co.uk}} After playing junior basketball for the [[Hackney White Heat]] of the [[English Basketball League]], Mensah-Bonsu moved to the United States where he spent his sophomore year of high school playing at the [[Hun School of Princeton]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]]. He then transferred to [[St. Augustine Preparatory School]] in [[Richland, New Jersey]] where as a senior in 2001–02, he averaged 15 points, 12 rebounds, and four blocks per game.{{Cite web |title=21 Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.gwsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pops_mensah_bonsu_227085.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712233006/http://www.gwsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pops_mensah_bonsu_227085.html |archive-date=12 July 2018 |access-date=31 August 2013 |website=GWSports.com}} ==College career== Mensah-Bonsu majored in [[psychology]] at [[George Washington University]], where he played [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] for the [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|Colonials men's basketball team]].{{Cite web |title=Pops Mensah-Bonsu College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/pops-mensah-bonsu-1.html |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} In his four-year career, he played 112 games (71 starts) while averaging 11.7 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks in 23.8 minutes per game. As a sophomore in 2003–04, he was named the Atlantic 10 Most Improved Player of the Year; as a junior in 2004–05, he was named to the All-Atlantic 10 second team; and as a senior in 2005–06, he was named to the All-Atlantic 10 first team and Atlantic 10 All-Defensive team. In the 2004–05 season, Mensah-Bonsu helped lead the Colonials to the [[2005 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2005 NCAA Tournament]], where they lost in the first round. The next season was more successful, with the team ending the regular season 26–1 and being ranked in the national top 10 for the first time in 50 years. However, he suffered a knee injury near the end of the regular season and he did not return until the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2006 NCAA Tournament]], where the injury lessened his production. After defeating [[University of North Carolina at Wilmington|UNC Wilmington]] in the first round, George Washington went on to lose to [[Duke University|Duke]] in the second round.{{Cite web |title=UNC Wilmington vs. George Washington Box Score, March 16, 2006 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2006-03-16-george-washington.html |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=George Washington vs. Duke Box Score, March 18, 2006 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2006-03-18-duke.html |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===2006–2007: Dallas Mavericks=== After going undrafted in the [[2006 NBA draft]], he joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the 2006 NBA Summer League. On 3 August 2006, he signed with the Mavericks.{{Cite web |date=4 August 2006 |title=Mavs hop on Pops, sign forward Mensah-Bonsu |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2538627 |access-date=4 August 2006 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Fort Worth Flyers]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. In the 2006–07 season, he managed just 12 games for the Mavericks, averaging 2.4 points and 1.8 rebounds in 5.9 minutes per game. In July 2007, Mensah-Bonsu re-joined the Mavericks for the 2007 NBA Summer League, but was later waived by the team on 31 August 2007.{{Cite web |date=31 August 2007 |title=Mavericks waive F Mensah-Bonsu |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=txmavericksmensahbonsu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305055353/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=txmavericksmensahbonsu |archive-date=5 March 2016 |access-date=31 August 2007 |website=Yahoo.com}} ===2007–2008: Benetton Treviso, Granada and Joventut Badalona=== [[File:Pops.jpg|150px|thumb|right|Mensah-Bonsu with [[Joventut Badalona]] in 2008]] In September 2007, Mensah-Bonsu signed a one-year deal with [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{Cite web |last=Dugdale |first=Rob |date=3 September 2007 |title=Mensah-Bonsu joins Italian team |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/other_sports/basketball/6973512.stm |access-date=3 September 2007 |website=BBC.co.uk}} In May 2008, Mensah-Bonsu signed with [[CB Granada]] of Spain for the team's final game of the season.{{Cite web |date=12 May 2008 |title=Pops, the Hero of Granada |url=http://colonialhoops.blogspot.com.au/2008/05/pops-hero-of-granada.html |access-date=12 May 2008 |website=BlogSpot.com.au}} In July 2008, Mensah-Bonsu initially joined the Dallas Mavericks for the 2008 NBA Summer League, but later joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] where he played four games and averaged 14.3 points per game.{{Cite web |title=2008 Timberwolves Summer League Team |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/team/index.jsp?team=timberwolves |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141014164130/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/team/index.jsp?team=timberwolves |archive-date=14 October 2014 |access-date=31 August 2013 |website=NBA.com}} On 15 August 2008, he signed a one-year deal with [[Joventut Badalona]].{{Cite web |date=15 August 2008 |title=MENSAH-BONSU OFFICIALLY SIGNS FOR BADALONA |url=http://www.gbbasketball.com/news/446.php |access-date=15 August 2008 |website=GBBasketball.com}}{{Cite web |date=16 July 2008 |title=DKV Joventut adds size with Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/33900/180/dkv-joventut-adds-size-with-pops-mensah-bonsu |access-date=16 July 2008 |website=Euroleague.net}} On 3 November 2008, he returned to the [[United States]] after injuring his shoulder playing for Joventut.{{Cite web |date=3 November 2008 |title=Joventut's Mensah-Bonsu out with shoulder injury |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/37401/180/joventut-s-mensah-bonsu-out-with-shoulder-injury |access-date=3 November 2008 |website=Euroleague.net}} A month later, he parted ways with Joventut to focus on recovery.{{Cite web |date=5 December 2008 |title=Joventut releases Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/40031/180/joventut-releases-mensah-bonsu |access-date=5 December 2008 |website=Euroleague.net}} ===2009–2011: NBA and NBA Development League=== On 28 January 2009, Mensah-Bonsu was acquired by the [[Austin Toros]] of the NBA Development League.{{Cite web |date=28 January 2009 |title=Toros Add Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/mensah_bonsu_090128.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090130122647/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/mensah_bonsu_090128.html |archive-date=30 January 2009 |access-date=28 January 2009 |website=NBA.com}} On 25 February 2009, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |date=25 February 2009 |title=Austin's Pops Mensah-Bonsu Called Up To San Antonio Spurs |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/mensah_bonsu_090225.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226220002/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/mensah_bonsu_090225.html |archive-date=26 February 2009 |access-date=25 February 2009 |website=NBA.com}} However, on 4 March 2009, he was released by the Spurs after appearing in just three games.{{Cite web |date=4 March 2009 |title=Spurs release Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=3701 |access-date=4 March 2009 |website=InsideHoops.com}} Two days later, he signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the rest of the 2008–09 season.{{Cite web |date=6 March 2009 |title=Austin's Pops Mensah-Bonsu Called Up To Toronto Raptors |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/mensah_bonsu_090306.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090309192429/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/mensah_bonsu_090306.html |archive-date=9 March 2009 |access-date=6 March 2009 |website=NBA.com}} On 29 June 2009, the Raptors extended a qualifying offer to Mensah-Bonsu in order to make him a restricted free agent.{{Cite web |date=30 June 2009 |title=GAME ON AT THE O2 – RAPTORS EXTEND QUALIFYING OFFER TO MENSAH-BONSU |url=http://www.gbbasketball.com/news/154.php |access-date=30 June 2009 |website=GBBasketball.com}} However, the Raptors later withdrew their qualifying offer on 7 July 2009. In August 2009, Mensah-Bonsu signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |date=24 August 2009 |title=Report: Rockets reach verbal deal with Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/08/20/mensah.rockets.ap/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013095626/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/08/20/mensah.rockets.ap/ |title=Rockets assign Dorsey to D-League, waive Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/11/13/rockets.moves.ap/ |access-date=13 November 2009 |website=NBA.com}} Four days later, he was claimed |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/11994/raptors-to-waive-mensah-bonsu |access-date=5 January 2010 |website=ESPN.com}} On 12 January 2010, Mensah-Bonsu signed with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of Russia for the rest of the 2009–10 season.{{Cite web |date=12 January 2010 |title=CSKA MOSCOW tabs Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006133215/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/euroleaguenews/transactions/2009-10-signings/i/64958/3694/cska-moscow-tabs-pops-mensah-bonsu |archive-date=6 October 2014 |access-date=12 January 2010 |website=Eurocupbasketball.com}} On 9 August 2010, Mensah-Bonsu signed a one-year deal (with the option of a second) with [[Saski Baskonia|Caja Laboral]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web |date=9 August 2010 |title=CAJA LABORAL lands Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2010-11-signings/i/74726/4465/caja-laboral-lands-mensah-bonsu |access-date=9 August 2010 |website=Euroleague.net}} He later left during pre-season for medical reasons. On 24 September 2010, he signed with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Jimmy |date=24 September 2010 |title=Jannero Pargo happy to rejoin Chris Paul with New Orleans Hornets |url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2010/09/jannero_pargo_happy_to_rejoin.html |access-date=24 September 2010 |website=NOLA.com}} On 4 January 2011, he was waived by the Hornets.{{Cite web |date=4 January 2011 |title=HORNETS WAIVE MENSAH-BONSU |url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_waive_pops_mensahbons_2011_01_04.html |access-date=4 January 2011 |website=NBA.com}} On 17 February 2011, Mensah-Bonsu signed with [[ASVEL Basket]] of France for the rest of the 2010–11 season.{{Cite web |date=17 February 2011 |title=ASVEL signs rebounding ace Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/85530/asvel-signs-rebounding-ace-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=17 February 2011 |website=Sportando.com}} ===2011–2012: Beşiktaş=== On 5 December 2011, Mensah-Bonsu signed with [[Beşiktaş men's basketball team|Beşiktaş]] of Turkey for the 2011–12 season.{{Cite web |date=5 December 2011 |title=Besiktas adds rebounding ace Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/89071/besiktas-adds-rebounding-ace-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=5 December 2011 |website=Sportando.com}} He went on to win the Turkish League championship, Turkish Cup, and the EuroChallenge. He was named the TBL Player of the Year. ===2012–2013: Sevilla and Olimpia Milano=== [[File:Croped pops632-Madrid-CB Sevilla marzo 2013.jpg|150px|thumb|left|Mensah-Bonsu with [[CB Sevilla|Cajasol Sevilla]] in 2013]] On 2 August 2012, Mensah-Bonsu signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web |date=2 August 2012 |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv adds forward Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/94146/maccabi-tel-aviv-adds-forward-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=2 August 2012 |website=Sportando.com}}{{Cite web |date=2 August 2012 |title=Maccabi Electra tabs veteran big man Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/99060/180/maccabi-electra-tabs-veteran-big-man-mensah-bonsu |access-date=2 August 2012 |website=Euroleague.net}} However, he was later waived by Maccabi on 19 September 2012 before appearing in a game for them after physicals showed he had not recovered from injuries picked up during the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|London Olympics]].{{Cite web |date=19 September 2012 |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv waives Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/95318/maccabi-tel-aviv-waives-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=19 September 2012 |website=Sportando.com}} On 4 March 2013, Mensah-Bonsu signed with [[CB Sevilla|Cajasol Sevilla]] of Spain for the rest of the 2012–13 season.{{Cite web |date=4 March 2013 |title=Cajasol officially signs Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/99660/cajasol-officially-signs-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=4 March 2013 |website=Sportando.com}} On 16 April 2013, he parted ways with Sevilla after managing just six games.{{Cite web |date=16 April 2013 |title=Cajasol-Pops officially part ways |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/100559/cajasol-pops-officially-part-ways.html |access-date=16 April 2013 |website=Sportando.com}} Two days later, he signed with [[Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]] of Italy for the rest of the season.{{Cite web |date=18 April 2013 |title=Olimpia Milano officially signs Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/100638/olimpia-milano-officially-signs-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=18 April 2013 |website=Sportando.com}} ===2013–2014: Galatasaray=== On 27 September 2013, Mensah-Bonsu signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |date=27 September 2013 |title=Wizards sign Josh Childress, Pops Mensah-Bonsu, Xavier Silas, D'Or Fischer to training camp |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14356 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715184312/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14356 |archive-date=15 July 2015 |access-date=27 September 2013 |website=InsideHoops.com}} However, he was later waived by the Wizards on 24 October 2013 after appearing in four preseason games.{{Cite web |date=24 October 2013 |title=Wizards waive Josh Childress, Pops Mensah-Bonsu, Xavier Silas |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14627 |access-date=24 October 2013 |website=InsideHoops.com}} Four days later, he signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray Liv Hospital]] of Turkey for the 2013–14 season.{{Cite news |date=28 October 2013 |title=GALATASARAY brings in Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/121395 |access-date=28 October 2013 |work=Euroleague.net}} On 31 October, he made his debut in a [[2013–14 Euroleague|Euroleague]] game against [[Unicaja Málaga]], in which he recorded 10 points and 11 rebounds.{{Cite web |date=31 October 2013 |title=Regular Season Round 3: Unicaja – Galatasaray 84–57 |url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Euroleague/2013/1031_138_328.asp |access-date=31 October 2013 |website=Eurobasket.com}} His time with the team was marred by an in-game fight with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] centre [[Mirza Begić]] on 28 November 2013.{{Cite web |date=28 November 2013 |title=Ρεκόρ και… ξύλο στο ΣΕΦ |url=http://www.efsyn.gr/?p=154855 |access-date=28 November 2013 |website=efsyn.gr |language=tr}} He was banned for three games and ordered fined €10,001.{{Cite web |date=4 December 2013 |title=Pops-Begic-Printezis fined, suspended. Olympiacos behind closed doors |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/108874/pops-begic-printezis-fined-suspended-olympiacos-behind-closed-doors.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006080301/http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/108874/pops-begic-printezis-fined-suspended-olympiacos-behind-closed-doors.html |archive-date=6 October 2014 |access-date=4 December 2013 |website=Sportando.com}} ===2014–2015: Hapoel Jerusalem and AEK Athens=== On 30 September 2014, Mensah-Bonsu joined with the [[Denver Nuggets]] training camp.{{Cite web |date=30 September 2014 |title=Denver Nuggets Announce 2014–15 Training Camp Roster |url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/denver-nuggets-announce-2014-15-training-camp-roster |access-date=30 September 2014 |website=NBA.com}} However, the next day, he left the Nuggets for personal reasons.{{Cite web |last=Scarito |first=Eddie |date=1 October 2014 |title=Pops Mensah-Bonsu Leaves Nuggets Camp |url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2014/10/mensah-leaves-nuggets.html |access-date=1 October 2014 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} On 20 November 2014, Mensah-Bonsu signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of Israel for the 2014–15 season.{{Cite news |date=20 November 2014 |title=Hapoel Jerusalem signs Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/141852/hapoel-jerusalem-signs-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |access-date=20 November 2014 |work=Sportando.com}} On 23 December 2014, he parted ways with Hapoel after appearing in two league games and four Eurocup games.{{Cite news |date=23 December 2014 |title=Hapoel Jerusalem, Pops Mensah-Bonsu part ways |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/145992/hapoel-jerusalem-pops-mensah-bonsu-part-ways.html |access-date=23 December 2014 |work=Sportando.com}} On 27 December 2014, he signed with [[A.E.K. Athens B.C.|AEK Athens]] for the rest of the [[2014–15 Greek Basket League]] season.{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2014 |title=AEK Athens signs Pops Mensah-Bonsu |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/146462/aek-athens-signs-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228042926/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/146462/aek-athens-signs-pops-mensah-bonsu.html |archive-date=December 28, 2014 |website=Sportando}} On 26 June 2015, Mensah-Bonsu was suspended for two years of any sports activity involvement after testing positive for amphetamines, which he claimed was from an approved, prescribed medicine.{{Cite news |date=26 June 2015 |title=Δύο χρόνια στον Μενσά Μπονσού |url=http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/OmadesBasket/A1Aek/duo-xronia-ston-mensa-mponsou.3548833.html |access-date=26 June 2015 |work=sport24.gr |language=el |archive-date=26 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626190639/http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/OmadesBasket/A1Aek/duo-xronia-ston-mensa-mponsou.3548833.html |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |last=Woods |first=Mark |date=26 June 2015 |title=POPS HANDED DOPING BAN |url=http://www.mvp247.com/2015/06/pops-doping-ban/ |website=mvp247.com}} ===The Basketball Tournament=== Mensah-Bonsu competed for [[Team City of Gods]] in [[The Basketball Tournament]]. He was a forward on the 2015 team that made it to the semifinals, losing to [[Overseas Elite]] 84–71.{{Cite news |last=Yates |first=Clinton |date=31 July 2015 |title=That's Mike Sweetney and Pops Mensah-Bonsu closing in on the $1M prize in The Basketball Tournament |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/dc-sports-bog/wp/2015/07/31/thats-mike-sweetney-and-pops-mensah-bonsu-closing-in-on-the-1m-prize-in-the-basketball-tournament/ |access-date=13 June 2022 |work=Washington Post |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Conner |first=Desmond |date=2 August 2015 |title=Overseas Elite Defeats Team 23 in $1M Basketball Tournament |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/basketball/hc-the-tournament-0803-20150802-story.html |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=Hartford Courant}} == National team career == [[File:Pops Mensah-Bonsu.jpg|thumb|right|Mensah-Bonsu with the [[Great Britain men's national basketball team|Great Britain national team]] at the [[2012 London Olympics]]]] Mensah-Bonsu earned 40 international caps for the [[Great Britain men's national basketball team|Great Britain men's national team]] between 2008 and 2012. He averaged 15.3 points and 8.8 rebounds per game during his international career. He recorded 14 double-doubles including a career best 32 points and 21 rebounds against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national basketball team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] on 26 August 2010.{{Cite web |last=Dugdale |first=Rob |date=26 August 2010 |title=GB qualify with win over Bosnia |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/other_sports/basketball/8948300.stm |access-date=27 July 2020 |website=BBC.co.uk |language=en-GB}} Mensah-Bonsu was part of the GB team that qualified for the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2009|2009 EuroBasket]]. During qualification, he averaged 12.2 points, 10 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game. He went on to join the British squad for their first appearance in the EuroBasket Tournament. The team lost all three of their first-round games but were competitive throughout including a very close game with world champions Spain. Mensah-Bonsu was again part of the British team in 2010 as they qualified for [[FIBA EuroBasket 2011]] with a 6–2 record. During qualification, he led all Division A players with 13.5 rebounds per game, and also finished sixth in points (19.3) and blocks (1.3). Mensah-Bonsu was selected for the final 12-man Great Britain roster for the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in London. He played in four games, recording 46 points and 29 rebounds. He missed Great Britain's final group game – a 90–58 win over [[China national basketball team|China]] – due to injury. Great Britain finished with a 1–4 record, failing to qualify for the knockout stage.{{Cite web |title=Pops Mensah Bonsu's profile |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/38650/sid/6232/tid/2791/tid2//_/2012_Olympic_Men/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006085304/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/38650/sid/6232/tid/2791/tid2//_/2012_Olympic_Men/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 October 2014 |access-date=1 October 2014 |website=FIBA.com}} ==Managerial career== On 14 October 2015, after receiving a two-year ban for doping, Pops announced retirement from professional basketball.{{Cite web |last=Carchia |first=E. |date=14 October 2015 |title=Pops Mensah-Bonsu retires from basketball |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/178706/pops-mensah-bonsu-retires-from-basketball.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151118130655/http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/178706/pops-mensah-bonsu-retires-from-basketball.html |archive-date=18 November 2015 |access-date=14 October 2015 |website=sportando.com}} He then began working as an Advanced Pro Scout for the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. On 7 August 2018, the [[Capital City Go-Go]], the new [[NBA G League]] affiliate of the [[Washington Wizards]], announced that Mensah-Bonsu had been made the team's first general manager.{{Cite web |last=Raim, Jacob |date=7 August 2018 |title=Capital City Go-Go Name Pops Mensah-Bonsu as GM and Jarell Christian as Head Coach |url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/capital-city-go-go-name-pops-mensah-bonsu-as-gm-and-jarell-christian-as-head-coach/ |url-status=dead December 2021 |access-date=11 August 2018 |website=capitalcity.gleague.nba.com}} He left the team in 2020.{{Cite news |last=Buckner |first=Candace |date=2 July 2020 |title=Pops Mensah-Bonsu will not
